status: exploratory Given extension design, unimplemented; AI-written JavaScript targeting workerd is the human-required implementation target; exact syntax and integration contract remain open
purpose: Describe local Given vocabulary in natural language and generate a saved JavaScript implementation, while Can continues to own declaring identity, schemas/interfaces and admitted behavior boundaries.

draft_syntax.definition: trait completable "Add done:bool=false with Status/Done/Open captions. Keep the existing authorized update path; add no operations or permission grants."
draft_syntax.use: Todo {title:text trim min=1 max=200 label="Task"} completable label="Todo"
draft_syntax.meaning: trait is the recommended replacement for implicit; completable is a local modifier name. It describes a reusable declaration extension, not inheritance or interface conformance. Exact spelling/application targets remain proposed.

example_expansion.generated_model: Todo { title:text trim min=1 max=200 label="Task", done:bool=false label={text="Status",values={true="Done",false="Open"}} } label="Todo"
example_expansion.retained_operation: crud Todo by=members fields=title,done label={create="Add task"}
example_expansion.scope: A completion flag and its captions/default only. The existing explicit CRUD update and its authority supply completion/reopening; the custom word alone grants neither access nor a new operation.

recommended_architecture: Saved AI-authored JavaScript ES modules targeting workerd, joined behind compiler-visible typed declaration/effect contracts in the normal application artifact. Canonical Can expansion may still supply schemas and supported declarative rules, but is not the only generated implementation output. Exact custom-JS extension seam is not designed or implemented.
ownership: Definition and explicit uses belong to their canonical declaring package/app owner. Only explicit applications expand. Preserve built-in defaults and reserved words; cross-package extension/export is not specified in this local draft.

behavior_boundary.given: Schemas/defaults/pure rules must remain visible through checked declarations or an explicit typed extension contract; JavaScript implementation alone does not define an invisible model or interface.
behavior_boundary.when: Operations/hooks/effects require declared entry points and a checked effects contract integrated with normal When/canonical execution. The exact custom-JS interface is open; no new API is assumed.
behavior_boundary.authority: Any generated policy/operation must expose its exact grants in the accepted expansion and use normal owner admission. Do not invent privileges from an adjective or bypass version, transaction, replay or evaluation semantics.
behavior_boundary.conflicts: Do not silently change explicit author declarations or shared language defaults. Diagnose unresolved/conflicting meaning or definitions before acceptance.
behavior_boundary.expressibility: Human steering permits AI-written workerd JS for custom behavior beyond simple canonical-source expansion. Define and implement the extension interface/effects/authority contract before claiming that behavior is supported; existing Can checks do not typecheck arbitrary JavaScript.
behavior_boundary.qualification: Can checks cover supported declarations. Generated JS needs interface checking plus relevant actual-workerd behavior checks; neither preflight nor an LLM judgement proves prose correspondence, permissions or sandboxing.

saved_generation.record: Accepted generated JavaScript and any required checked declaration/interface metadata, with declaring definition/use identity, relevant inputs, effective generator provider/model/recipe and target runtime configuration. Exact record/discovery mechanism remains open.
saved_generation.ordinary_builds: Consume current tracked JavaScript/required interface metadata without AI; validate source/contract/target compatibility. Direct code edits are allowed. Generator configuration changes affect future attempts without replacing otherwise compatible current code.
saved_generation.controls: Use the unified controls catalog in design/proposals/build-generation/proposal.json, including direct file editing, current-code refine, finite retry, conditional candidate promotion and reset preserving current edits.
saved_generation.schema_changes: Accepting generated stored schema changes still uses the existing schema evolution/migration workflow; regeneration does not itself migrate deployed records.
saved_generation.agent: Can-aware semantic profile resolved by proposed root tooling settings, CLI-first; exact backend default/provider/model remains unselected. frontend remains the default logical Then role.
saved_generation.operator: AI authoring agent uses structured CLI discovery, concrete files and callable validation/acceptance; no mandatory human-facing UI or review flow. See the unified operator contract.

current_evidence.grammar: docs/specification/GRAMMAR.md currently forbids arbitrary extension words; compiler/src/syntax/parser.rs has closed Given dispatch plus model declaration syntax.
current_evidence.pipeline: compiler/src/analysis/mod.rs check_program owns normal parse/resolution/type/effect/example/source checks; compiler/src/cli.rs emits after analysis.
current_evidence.existing_semantics: docs/specification/DESIGN.md sections 2-4 specify defaults, policies, invariants/locks, authority and evaluation behavior.
current_evidence.js_runtime: compiler/src/codegen/js.rs emits appDefinition/canApp registries; runtime/invoke.ts resolves declared registry members under canonical admission; deploy/bundle.ts creates the portable workerd module map; dev/local-run.ts uses Miniflare with the selected compatibilityDate.
current_evidence.missing_seam: No supported authored custom-Given AI-JS extension registration/API was found. Existing artifact import/syntax checks and version/capability preflight do not prove arbitrary JS semantics or isolate its authority.
current_evidence.node_compatibility_reference: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/nodejs/; current official docs distinguish supported/partial APIs and non-functional import stubs, with compatibility settings controlling availability.

advice.interpretation: Historical advice favored canonical expansion under the earlier bounded model-field outcome. Human steering now requires AI-written workerd JavaScript; these results do not decide or qualify its new integration interface, and do not override that requirement.

runtime_target.runtime: workerd, using the selected application compatibility date/flags and supported bindings
runtime_target.producer: The build-time coding agent can write the implementation directly. Existing compiler-emitted JS remains the path for ordinary supported Can constructs.
runtime_target.packaging: Persist accepted generated module bytes and effective generator identity; bundle those modules through the existing portable Worker artifact path rather than evaluating a prompt or generating code on requests.
runtime_target.apis: Use only APIs and dependencies supported by the selected workerd configuration. Do not assume a module that imports or runs under Node also functions in workerd.
runtime_target.execution: Integrate through a defined Can interface/effects boundary so canonical admission, declared grants, transaction commit, failure/replay and exact value representations remain owned by the existing runtime. Generated code must not silently establish separate direct-storage authority.
runtime_target.qualification: Syntax/import preflight plus direct loading and relevant behavior checks in the actual workerd host. Type/interface checking must be designed for generated JS; current Can checks do not establish arbitrary JS correctness or isolation.
runtime_target.status: Target accepted as a human requirement; no generated JS module or new extension registration exists.

direction: Human now confirms introducing build-time generation across Given/When/Then; shared catalog and remaining interfaces are in design/proposals/build-generation/proposal.json.
